blockers.title: Integrity lockdown still permits a signed but undeclared executing kernel
evidence: The carried exact-byte-delivery requirement mandates a closed platform base/host-ABI TCB: every permitted OS ABI has an allowlist identity rule, undeclared resolution or identity drift refuses, and hostile clean machines prove that no ambient system dependency enters silently.

fromBootLockdown requires measured Boot#### OptionalData to contain lockdown=integrity and the present lockdown sysfs token to select integrity. Its own role expressly says this addresses unsigned kexec only and does not authenticate a signed kexec of a different kernel. linuxStanding and g22 repeat that signed replacement remains residual and disclosed.

Signature acceptance is not identity equality to authenticatedKernelMember. A kernel M signed by a key the running kernel accepts for kexec can have different bytes, version, package, and host-ABI behavior from allowlisted K. Integrity lockdown may admit M because it is signed; no v33 rule compares M to authenticatedKernelMember.sha256, peCoffImageDigest, package identity, or any other signed OS-ABI entry.

Concrete counterexample: firmware launches allowlisted K with the measured lockdown option; K enters integrity mode; a privileged actor uses the signed-kexec path to enter different signed M; M also exposes integrity lockdown; qualification obtains a fresh TPM quote. The quote and transcript still authenticate the firmware launch of K, fromBootLockdown passes, buildIdDriftDetector cannot refuse, runtimeContinuity is optional hardening, and NT-TCB-DISCLOSE-KEXEC is not a pass/fail cell. M is nevertheless the kernel implementing the actual host ABI.

NT-TCB-1 says an undeclared object on an active complete profile refuses and that inability to observe it requires qualification failure or a platform-removal path. The disclosure says signed M is outside the bind, must not be treated as NT-TCB-1 inapplicability, and is not a Linux withdrawal. Linux remains mandatory in slice 1. The same internal contradiction identified in PTCB-V32-B1 therefore remains for every signed replacement.

The SHOULD-level G22 suggestion to use machines with kexec unavailable is explicitly not proof. v33 does not require kexec to be unavailable, disable all kexec monotonically, restrict accepted kexec images to the exact signed inventory, or authenticate the current image. fromBootLockdown is useful hardening but not the required no-replacement or current-identity proof.
blockers.impact: A Linux machine can qualify boot-time K evidence while executing signed, undeclared M. The current OS-ABI TCB remains open, so NT-TCB-1/NT-TCB-3 and the hostile-clean-machine property admit a false allow despite the new lockdown condition.
blockers.requiredRepair: To keep Linux in slice 1, close both unsigned and signed replacement. Either authenticate the currently executing kernel with independently rooted, event-bound evidence and compare its exact cryptographic identity to a permitted OS-ABI entry, or attest and enforce a monotonic no-replacement policy that disables every kexec path before replacement can be staged and through observedAt. If signed kexec remains available, its accepted image identity must be restricted and measured against the same signed inventory; signature validity alone is insufficient. A disclosure cannot replace this pass/fail closure.

shouldFix.title: fromBootLockdown does not define the load-option parse or prove that the measured token established enforcement
evidence: optionalDataToken says the authenticated Boot#### UEFI_VARIABLE_DATA VariableData (load-option OptionalData) MUST contain the 8-bit token lockdown=integrity. Boot#### VariableData is the complete load-option byte sequence, but the contract supplies no EFI_LOAD_OPTION parse that locates OptionalData after its attributes, description, and FilePathList.

Contain is not a closed command-line grammar. No encoding, delimiter, token-boundary, duplicate/override, termination, or exact-effective-command-line rule is defined. Different validators can accept a substring inside unrelated or non-effective OptionalData, or disagree whether the bytes are the Linux EFI-stub command line at all.

The measured token proves only that bytes occurred in the boot variable. The contract does not require a signed property that authenticated K implements the named parameter and denies unsigned kexec under that configuration. lockdownNow is read after any possible transition from whichever kernel is currently executing, so it does not by itself attest K's enforcement interval.

The live inScopeBootConfigs, refusesBootConfigs, and unavailableRefuses summaries were not updated to name the new token/parser or absent-lockdown failure, while linuxStanding and the nested field make it mandatory. The nested MUSTs establish refusal, but the profile summary is incomplete.
shouldFix.impact: Implementations can disagree on which Boot#### bytes satisfy the new mandatory field and can record the claimed unsigned no-replacement property without a defined causal or feature binding to K.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define the exact EFI_LOAD_OPTION parser, the canonical OptionalData encoding accepted by the directly launched Linux EFI stub, token boundaries and duplicate/override semantics, and equality to the effective kernel command line. Bind the authenticated K entry to a required lockdown/kexec-enforcement capability or an independently attested policy, and propagate missing/malformed/ineffective lockdown to the governing in-scope and refusal clauses.

advisories.title: DIGEST-BOUND-only pre-kernel joins need an explicit taxonomy disposition for loader and framework code
evidence: v33 correctly preserves a four-field signedEntry row and limits non-kernel codeBearing evidence to DIGEST-BOUND so the joined digest is the measured code digest.

The unchanged classMap permits loader and framework entries only as PLATFORM-ATTESTED, while codeBearing includes application, driver, IPL, and non-host-code event types that can represent those classes. Such a correctly classified row has no lawful DIGEST-BOUND signedEntry under the present map.
The direct EFI-stub profile may intend to refuse every non-kernel loader/framework event and use comparable system-class dependency for firmware code, but that scope rule is not stated.
advisories.suggestedRepair: State that this profile refuses non-kernel loader/framework rows and define the lawful class mapping for firmware code, or add a class-appropriate DIGEST-BOUND identity route for measured pre-kernel loader/framework bytes.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this review finds 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX finding.
conclusion: REJECT. v33 removes the stale currentExecution sentence, preserves every non-kernel code signedEntry join while waiving only byte reconstruction, fixes the G22 status wording, and adds authenticated lockdown hardening. It still does not close the current Linux OS ABI: integrity lockdown admits a signed but different kernel M, signature validity is not equality to the signed K entry, and v33 expressly leaves M in a non-pass/fail disclosure while retaining Linux as mandatory. The new Boot#### token also lacks a closed load-option/effective-command-line and enforcement binding. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains in D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
